title: Debounce regional drain fanout and throttle control-plane drain propagation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Postmortem for a multi-region routing incident where simultaneous drain signals from nodes in us-west-2 caused a control-plane broadcast that triggered cascading fallbacks and mass model-variant swaps. This ticket captures timeline, root cause, immediate mitigations, and long-term changes (debounce/throttle logic in control-plane, dashboarding, and testing).
impact_summary: During a 22-minute window on 2025-02-10 we observed elevated error rates and 3x latency for tiered customers in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 because the routing plane propagated dozens of near-simultaneous drain tombstones. Smart routing reacted by failing over requests to fallback model variants and higher-cost tiers, causing throughput reduction and increased cost. Customer-facing errors peaked at ~12% for a subset of routes.
timeline: 2025-02-10T09:03:00Z - Automated node health check change (rollout of health-check tuning) completed in us-west-2.
2025-02-10T09:06:12Z - Spike of node transients; ~38 nodes reported short-lived unhealthy->drain in <90s.
2025-02-10T09:07:05Z - Control-plane accepted and broadcasted drain tombstones without rate limiting; route recomputation started.
2025-02-10T09:07:40Z - Smart routing policy detected capacity shortfall and triggered variant fallbacks and tier escalation across multiple regions.
2025-02-10T09:09:00Z - Error rates climb; on-call SRE notified via pager.
2025-02-10T09:12:30Z - Mitigation: traffic steering rules applied to pin critical routes to unaffected regions and manual suppression of drain broadcasts.
2025-02-10T09:25:00Z - Traffic normalized after targeted rollback of health-check tuning and reversion of aggressive drain tombstones.
2025-02-10T09:25:30Z - Full service metrics back to baseline; incident declared resolved at 09:30Z.
root_cause: A change to the per-node health-check aggressiveness created a burst of short-lived health flaps. The control-plane currently treats drain tombstones as high-priority immediate state and broadcasts them to all routing shards with eventual consistency. There was no debouncing of multiple drain reports for the same rack/region and no control-plane rate limit for tombstone propagation, so a single failure mode produced a fanout amplification that combined with policy-driven automatic fallbacks to cause cascading variant swaps and cross-region failovers.
mitigations_taken: Rolled back the health-check tuning in us-west-2 to the previous stable configuration (rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/11284).
Applied temporary suppression on the routing control-plane to ignore drain tombstones if duplicate within 60s for the same rack (hotfix: https://github.com/redwood/routing/pull/11320).
Pinned critical customer routes to specific regions to avoid automated fallback for 20 minutes while the system stabilized.
Added emergency alerting for drain-fanout-rate (Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/DR1/drain-fanout-overview).
Post-incident communication to affected customers and internal stakeholders; customer success followed up with impacted accounts.
long_term_fixes: Implement debounce logic in control-plane: coalesce drain tombstones per rack/az for a configurable window (default 30s) before global broadcast.
Add per-region and global rate limits for control-plane tombstone propagation with backpressure signals to serving runtime.
Introduce circuit-breaker in smart routing policy that prevents >N simultaneous variant swaps per region within M minutes (configurable policy).
Add e2e chaos tests to the routing-test-harness that simulate burst drain signals and assert no cascading fallbacks.

Update runbooks: incident playbook section 'drain-fanout' with runbook steps, dashboards to inspect, and rollback checklist (runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REINF/Drain+Fanout+Runbook).
Permanent metrics: drain_fanout_rate, tombstone_coalesce_ratio, and variant_swap_count_by_region (alerts for sustained abnormality).
